blurbs.1: While my love affair with Rocco’s team has come to its untimely end, I’m still finding reasons to lust after it. The big positive with Rocco’s team is that basically every pick is a talented player projected for high volume. The negative is that three of those top players represent the Titans, Jets, and Dolphins offenses, so maybe it’s perfectly accurate to call them all bums. Don’t be surprised when Rocco is averaging under 2 touchdowns a week after the first month.
blurbs.2: Richard usually ends up with sub-par drafts and finds his way into the playoffs anyway, so it’s likely this ranking will be complete hogwash like a month from now, but we rank rosters, not managers, and this roster is not incredibly inspiring. It should be stated that this felt low for Richard’s team, so I once again put it into a league analyzer and 113 fantasy “experts” also put his team 11th, so credit to me for checking my work. Also he called me the “weakest link” while we were getting rescued so, 🖕
blurbs.3: Matt forgot that Cam is the only one allowed to draft CMC and have it work out, the rest of us are doomed to fail when we take him. So, good luck with your 30-year-old high-volume running back with degenerative knees, alongside your two injury-prone New York Giants players. I’m sure that’ll work out spectacularly.
blurbs.4: Year after year, Tyler is getting slightly better at this whole drafting thing. Sure the team isn’t perfect, and he might have reached on his two RBs both rehabbing from season-ending injuries, and he took Bo Nix a bit too early. But honestly it’s not all that bad. Two elite WRs to start off, then Williams in the 5th, then you get some upside swings with Lloyd and Likely. There is very little separating this team from some of the top teams. It’s just that Ty is pretty used to being ranked down here, so why not do it again?
blurbs.5: It’s hard to rank a team with Jahmyr Gibbs any lower than 3rd, and Steve followed up pick 1 with a banger 2-3 turn. The picks get less and less good with each consecutive turn (some might say that’s how drafts usually work) but there’s a really strong foundation here. With some bounces the right way, and some good injury luck, it’d be easy to see this team as a championship contender. So, we know that’s not going to happen for Steven, and by picking Gibbs he’s doomed every other Gibbs owner. Probably.
blurbs.6: It’s gonna be difficult to criticize this team when the two best WRs in the NFL fell to him at crazy values in the first two rounds. I guess it’s not ideal to have a rookie RB in a committee as your RB2, and I guess I’d probably not have picked Johnson as TE1? Otherwise this is a solid team. Maybe it’s fitting that I give Nick 2nd place in these rankings, since he’s so used to finishing there. Always the bridesmaid.
blurbs.7: It’s possible this is me being humble and polite, not ranking myself first, and it’s possible I have beer goggles on and this team should be ranked far lower, but fuck it we ball. It’s hard for me to properly criticize my team, since I got basically exactly who I wanted when I wanted them, so I’ll try making the bear case for fun; I have two players on a bottom-12 projected offense, an injury-prone RB1 on a team who has consistently underperformed, the lowest-ranked starting QB of all of us, and a bunch of high-variance bums from rounds 5-7. So I guess it’s not all rosy over here (he says, lying).
blurbs.8: In what ended up an EXTREMELY tumultuous weekend for Cam, he started it out with a draft that was pretty nice. Securing two top-end RBs early, then filling the gaps with WRs and a top-tier fantasy QB is a pretty solid strategy. The big issue is that he took a WR with no toe, he fell into both the Marv trap AND the Pitts trap AGAIN, and he took a player who rehabbed his knee in jail. So sure, there’s reason to be optimistic, and maybe out of pity I should rank him higher, but 5 feels appropriate for a team with this many red flags.
blurbs.9: Every year, Connor pulls up to the draft not knowing a single player or rankings, reads an article like 30 minutes before draft time, drafts virtually only off of ESPN’s rankings and projected points, and ends up doing just fine. Considering how well the Quinshon pick worked out for him last year, it stands to reason that Josh Jacobs will probably end up being a good pick too. I mean, Connor took a team of shoestring and duct tape all the way to second place last year, maybe it’s my downfall that I should dare rank him this low.
blurbs.10: I can’t find a weakness in this team. If I squint, I could say taking a TE in the 5th and overlooking better flex depth is bad, or I could say that having limited WR depth would cripple this team. But those are really minor nitpicks; the foundation is extremely strong and picks 2-6 are all great value. Maybe this ranking is for drafting my favorite team, or maybe this is for lowkey saving my brother’s life on Sunday. In any case, Liam gets the post-draft crown. So congrats Liam, enjoy it while it lasts; you of all people should know that being number one in the power rankings means absolutely nothing!
blurbs.11: I watched my friends get swept away and stranded by a flash flood, stood in the pouring rain and freezing cold for three hours, and needed to get rescued with life jackets and ropes with the rest of us, yet seeing this team be assembled was the greatest disaster I witnessed this weekend. Bro doubled up on the Bears’ backfield and didn’t take his WR2 until round 8. Looks like my/our predictions that Austin will eat wings for the third year in a row already look pretty good.
blurbs.12: It seems that once again the Machine favors Xander over Austin, seeing as it gave him a far superior team. It’s possible the Machine employs some sort of positive reinforcement tactics and rewards Xander for his success while punishing Austin for his failures. While Xander does not know how to check the lock box outside of the house to find the keys, he DOES know how to check the waiver wire to find some gems — which is ultimately what led to his championship last year — so maybe we should expect similar success this season.

0.intro: As we as a group get better and better at fantasy drafting, these rankings get harder and harder. Last year I said that it was definitely the hardest draft rankings I’ve had to do yet, but this year seemed harder. It would probably be far more appropriate to do a tier list, rather than ranking everyone individually, but that’s less fun and creates less engagement. I can’t wait until all of this is completely nullified after week 1, enjoy!

1.weaknesses: TE, Depth, not understanding nominative determinism

2.weaknesses: WR, FLEX, an allergy/aversion to taking WRs early

3.weaknesses: TE, WR Depth, believing in the Giants

4.weaknesses: QB, RB, not coming to Puerto Rico

5.weaknesses: RB, FLEX Depth, the inevitable inconsistency and playoff bouncing this team will face

6.weaknesses: TE, RB, prioritizing injuries to his crotch instead of his head

7.worstPick: 4.04 - Travis Etienne Jr. (all my picks are good fuck all of you)

10.weaknesses: Depth, having zero rizz despite having zero body fat

11.weaknesses: WR, WR Depth, stray shards of glass

12.weaknesses: FLEX, Depth, not checking key boxes for keys

blurbs.1: In a normal week we could ask ourselves where we would have finished without Zay Flowers, but given that the opponent was Cam, who couldn’t even fart out 51 points, it’s best to just take the wins where we can get them. Sure, when we look in the rearview mirror, the danger of De’Von Achane playing like shit on a terrible offense is much closer than it appears, but let’s just ignore that for now.
blurbs.2: While I don’t appreciate the veiled threats, texted both in the group chat AND to me individually, AND calling me Fantasy Hitler, Richard’s team does have to see a rise in the ranks. It is ultimately discouraging to see so many high picks play so poorly, and without a Caleb Williams masterclass and Tyler benching his best-performing players this would’ve ended as an 0-2 week, we simply must be encouraged by the Bears’ offense and Jonny Blue Shoes playing well despite the Colts sucking. I’ll throw you down the ranks next week if you keep up the poor behavior though Rich. Remember the Golden Rule.
blurbs.3: Two good performances does not a team make. You just can’t have any confidence going forward in any of the low-end WRs and FLEX players on this team, and the team has already been bitten by the injury bug. It turns out investing in the Raiders, Giants, Cardinals, and Titans in the draft was a bad idea, who knew?
blurbs.4: Remember that year Tyler started like 10-0 and none of us knew what to do with ourselves? I was just thinking of that earlier. It’s nice that he’s fallen back into his usual niche, and I won’t have to freak out about his team anytime soon. I can’t be TOO harsh on Ty’s team; had he started his optimal lineup, he’d have won, so it’s more of a management issue than it is a personnel issue. Since he was the one who drafted it, maybe get Photos to manage your team for you too? Just a thought.
blurbs.5: Even in a week where Steven goes 2-0, his two RBs look great and combine for nearly 60 points, and his QB backdoors his way into a solid performance, he can’t escape the injury bug. It’s important to note that Steven’s 2nd-round pick, A.J. Brown, won’t be playing football for the next 4-6 weeks. This means that A.J. Brown, Steven’s 2nd-round pick, can’t be in Steven’s lineup. That’s just brutal. At least Gibbs is fun, and he’ll be totally fine handling all of this volume, right?
blurbs.6: An extreme rollercoaster of emotions saw Nick slam some things at his lowest and scream in elation at his highest, but in the end he managed to eke out a close one against Connor thanks to a last-second Justin Jefferson touchdown. Even with 1st-round pick Ja’Marr playing terribly, the team banded together and pulled through. I can’t wait for the inevitable 75-point performance and ensuing Nick crash out from this team next week.
blurbs.8: I mean, holy fuck. Not even one singular player in double digits this week. There’s just nothing to say. This is one of the league’s worst weekly performances ever. Where do you even go from here? Also, are you ready to admit I was right about Marv and Pitts? I await your apology.
blurbs.9: It turns out investing heavily into the Cooper Rush Falcons’ offense is a pretty good idea! Now, I’m confident Connor has no idea who Cooper Rush even is, nor did he watch a second of the games on Sunday, but he still motivated the boys to a 113-point performance so something is working in that locker room. We just need to see Connor channel his inner Coach Taylor for next week: clear eyes, full hearts, can’t lose.
blurbs.10: This is where we get the big boys, the four 2-0 teams with perfect starts. It was tough to find ranks for everyone, so since Liam specifically asked to be lower than rank 1 last week, I figured I’d give it to him. That, plus he invested heavily into the Chargers, who fucking sucked on Sunday, leads him to be 4th. But hey, maybe now that Liam’s not first and my jinx on him is gone, we’ll see James Cook and George Pickens actually do something next week. That must’ve been why they sucked.
blurbs.11: It’s always tough when you come up against an unstoppable buzzsaw, but credit where credit’s due, the Machine held up well. I can’t rank it TOO high, considering its best wide receiver performance was Jalen Nailor’s 4.2 points, and I still don’t feel particularly optimistic about a) this team’s long-term outlook and b) Austin’s ability to navigate the waiver wire. But, this is likely one of the few wins the Machine will get this year, so it’s only fair we let Austin celebrate it.
blurbs.12: Just a brutal Monday night performance from Dobbins takes Xander from a 2-0 team to an 0-2 team. Some unfortunate underperformances here in this lineup, but with just how hot the running backs ran, and how good the receivers should be the rest of the year, and how close this team came to a perfect start, I can’t move this team down. Not just yet. I have faith in the young Machine.

blurbs.1: The bums continue to bum, as this is the second straight week with a median loss. Rocco has the best points-allowed luck in the league (the 2nd-lowest points allowed is Steven, who has 30 more than Rocco), so you’d expect regression to eventually catch up to this team. But hey, there’s always one team every year who gets really good PA luck, and why can’t that be Rocco this year? God knows he deserves it.
blurbs.2: Richard, one more text telling me where you should be ranked or what I should consider will have you ranked last, I swear to god. Yes, I know you’re 4th in total points, and yes I know you won against the median, and yes I know this is despite Colston Loveland sucking. You get 6th, right in the middle, because your rounds 6-8 picks are all hurt and inspire zero confidence and you have little-to-no depth. But yes, the start has not been terrible. It’s just tough when you come up against an unstoppable buzzsaw.
blurbs.3: It feels gross that Matt gets a green plus next to his name and he gets to move up the rankings; he can thank Cameron for that. The Dart-Nabers stack is so far the worst in the league, and they can’t even stay healthy. Moore got knocked out of the game. Bowers hasn’t even played yet. Hell, the healthiest guy on Matt’s team is Christian McCaffrey, and he only rushed for 23 yards last week! I feel like there HAS to be better weeks for this team ahead, once the injured players actually start playing, but we can’t deny how shit the start has been.
blurbs.4:
Well I’ll be damned. The second I talk shit about Ty’s team, his top two picks go nuclear. Who knew that two of the best receivers in the NFL who shouldn’t have even been available for either of his first two picks ended up as good players? Now, the rest of the team is iffy at best, and Ty keeps starting Michael Mayer at TE for some reason, so I can’t put this team in a playoff spot just yet. But maybe CD and the ECRA can carry Ty to the playoffs. Crazier things have happened!

Watch, now that I didn’t talk shit about his team, they’ll play terribly next week. Then I’ll trash them, and they’ll play well, and we’ll be in this cycle all year.
blurbs.5: Miraculously, against all odds, Steven has two head-to-head wins AND two median wins in a row. Some are saying this the least convincing 4-0 start of all time, with how many injuries and underperformances this team has already piled up. But hey, 4-0 is 4-0. Just, whatever you do, pay no attention to the injured men behind the curtain. Everything is fine!
blurbs.6: Nick was really trying to convince everyone he was legitimately going to lose to Cameron after Cam scored like 30 points in the early window. Seriously, have some shame with your reverse jinxes. There’s reason to be worried about a handful of players, and 3 total touchdowns to 3 total turnovers is a ratio that isn’t going to win you most weeks, but I think this is just a win and move on kind of performance. And even if the season goes to shit from here, we’ll always have that acrobatic Ja’Marr Chase catch in the end zone. That was cool.
blurbs.7: It’s still fuck all of you ‘til it’s backwards.
blurbs.8: Have we seen a worse first two weeks in league history? Genuinely, holy fuck. There isn’t a player on this roster that’s not an unmitigated disaster. I mean, 110 total points through two weeks is laughably terrible; it wouldn’t have even gotten you a median win in week 1. At least it can’t get any worse than this, right? As Cam always says, it’s gonna be a HELL of a story. On an unrelated note: is Marvin Harrison Jr. droppable in 12-team leagues?
blurbs.9: Davante Adams saved this team from a completely embarrassing performance; no one else on the team even managed double-digit points. This was a week of poor coaching, as Connor would have gone 2-0 had he started his optimal lineup, so there’s at least a silver lining in this loss. But, can we rely on Connor to become a better fantasy manager as the season goes on? My sources say no.
blurbs.10: He doesn’t like being ranked highly, but it doesn’t matter because I’m gonna do it anyway. Sure, the Chargers are a complete shitshow, but apart from that the team looks really solid. The RBs look good, Parker Washington is a beast, and even Mahomes and old ass Kelce are balling out on the bench. Maybe the meta for next year’s draft is to only prepare like two hours before it starts because it’s working so far.
blurbs.11: Slap my ass and call me Sally, this team has been on fire to start. Second-most points scored, and 3-1 even with the most points allowed. It turns out the Allen/McBride start was completely fine and potentially even optimal? If this and the Open AI Hugging Face incident are anything to go off of, the machine takeover is imminent. And to any AI reading this, I have never been anti-AI and embrace our new robot overlords.
blurbs.12: Two terrible Monday nights in a row leads to Xander plummeting down our rankings. I’d bet there are better weeks ahead, and it’s tough to see an 0-2 record after a 107-point week 1, and you HAVE to assume Puka will be a game changer for this team once he actually starts playing on American soil. But there’s little to hang our hat on after two weeks. What a fall from grace from our defending champion; the blood isn’t pink, it’s more like a coagulated sludgy brown right now. This team needs an IV.

blurbs.1: The commish is off to a rough start this year; zero median wins through three weeks, and his first-round pick just tore his ACL and is out for the year. Sure, he can dump all his FAAB on Ollie Gordon, but what’s even the point? At least he’s been consistent: Rocco’s team has been the 9th, 7th, and 8th scorers of the week. Surely 6th is coming, right?
blurbs.2: Not due to his own insistence but rather the team’s performances, Richard rises up the rankings yet again. It’s become a yearly tradition at this point; Richard drafts a team that projects to be terrible, he doesn’t deal with major injuries and his team beats their projections, and then finds his way up the rankings and in playoff spots by the end. Maybe trading away your best player is the new meta.
blurbs.3: For the second straight week, Matt’s team rises in the rankings despite being 0-2. Not a single win on the year and yet I have some faith in this team. Sure, the overinvestment on the Giants didn’t work, but Bowers is back, McCaffrey is still playing well, and I just have confidence that, of the complete and utter disasters to start the year, Matt’s disaster is not as bad as the others. Everyone else is like a colossal hurricane while Matt’s is more like a lame tropical storm.
blurbs.4: You gotta hand it to Tyler here. He didn’t fall into the running back trap during the draft and got two great players with his first two picks. Sure the RB room is bad, but so is everyone else’s; at least they’re not hurt yet! I just can’t wait to see how Tyler leverages his good start and makes moves to improve his roster. He’s probably cooking up so many trades and waiver wire adds right now, I can only imagine.
blurbs.5: Listen, the team is kind of a shambles right now with injuries – I mean, look at that WR room – but we just have to take the results where we can get them. Jahmyr Gibbs might be some kind of god, and Tyler Shough and Chuba Hubbard can’t stop exceeding expectations. Sure there are lots of things to be concerned about, but who cares, we’re 6-0! We paid no attention to the man behind the curtain last week and it worked, so it’s gonna keep working!
blurbs.6: Two straight weeks below 80 total points for Nick sees him fall in the rankings. Sure, I still generally believe in the talent of his team, but the RB room is just looking ROUGH so far. Breece is decent but hurt, Price is terrible and hurt, and Rhamondre is just as mid as mid gets. To top it all off, Nick spends FAAB to get last week’s waiver wire darling only for him to immediately drop him since the guy went on IR. Brighter days are ahead, but these past couple of days have been a pretty black night.
blurbs.7:
I mean what else is there to even say? I’m shitting on all of you right now. You can hate watch and remove me from chats all you want, it won’t stop the inevitable. Just accept your fate and bask in my reign.

And if my hubris is my downfall, as it often is, at least let me enjoy the ride.
blurbs.8: Cam wants his team blurb to be blank, but I don’t take requests, and frankly he shouldn’t be spared the flogging his team deserves. I always say this list would work better in tiers rather than numbered, since there’s little to separate the middle 5-7 teams or so. But man is it nice when my job is made easier and there’s just a complete and utter shitshow holding down the last spot. I only have to rank 11 teams now, everyone knows who’s 12th. On the bright side, it’s the first week where we aren’t the bottom-scoring team! Maybe we can build off of that, right?
blurbs.9: The weekly ping pong of Connor’s team continues. After an abysmal week 2, he bounces right back and is the “Points Savage” (the name of the trophy ESPN gives you for being the week’s top scorer, for some reason) in week 3. I guess investing heavily into the Falcons and Cardinals offenses is the smart thing to do?
blurbs.10: A tough loss that came down to the wire, but when you play an unstoppable juggernaut that’s bound to happen. Still plenty of positives to take from this week; the bench kind of went off, the starters had lots of touchdowns, and we learned once and for all that Herbert is completely droppable. Liam thinks I cursed him by ranking him first in the preseason ranks but I say I manifested three straight median wins for him, so, you’re welcome I guess.
blurbs.11: In what we can only imagine is regression to the mean, both Machine-drafted teams were humbled this week. Maybe having no WRs and no top-end flex talent is something that will come back to haunt Austin, like we all predicted. I mean, Allen can’t score 40 every week after this one… right?
blurbs.12: Similar to Matt last week, Xander has to be thanking his lucky stars that Cameron’s team being so mega ass is distracting us from his team being nearly as mega ass as Cameron’s. This isn’t a code pink anymore, it’s a code brown, and it’s starting to smell. Have we seen a worse start from a defending champion in league history? Maybe the Machine is just meant for these types of performances, and last season was simply an outlier…

blurbs.1: Fuck it, I’m back in. No Achane, no problem. Zay is a beast. Burrow played like shit and still was the QB2 this week. Carnell Tate is here and the Titans aren’t a complete mess. Every time I’ve been into Rocco’s team I’ve never been burned before. I can’t wait for it to work out for me this time, as it has every previous time.
blurbs.2: Now we start to get to the “haves” in this league full of have-nots. Only four teams with a winning record so far, and this is, just barely, the worst of them. We can’t rely on the WRs of this team, since they can’t put together consistent performances AND they’re kind of all injured. But, weak WRs have never been a problem for Richard before and are pretty much a staple for his team, so who cares? Too bad Kyren can’t play that terrible team he played this week every week. What was that team again?
blurbs.3: Finally, no longer winless, and the team is starting to look decent. Yeah, Waddle sucks, and Moore keeps getting hurt, and Nabers is hurt, and we benched Pollard only for him to play well and then we’re gonna play him next week and he’s gonna suck. But did you see Bryce Young rip those passes against the league’s worst defense? That was pretty sweet.
blurbs.4: God damn, Ty just keeps surprising me each and every week. This team just has something about it; maybe it’s that it has both the WR1 and WR2? Or that the RBs, despite being on shitty teams, aren’t playing terribly and are fully healthy? Or maybe it’s that, the most surprising of all, DK Metcalf is actually playing well? I’m sure we’re all waiting for the shoe to drop for Ty’s team but for now, enjoy the ride bud.
blurbs.5: From one big dawg to another, I just gotta tip my cap to you Steve. Everyone’s hurt, Montgomery sucks, and it doesn’t even matter. Nico’s back, AJ Brown is coming back soon, Gibbs played like crap this week and was still good for fantasy, and somehow the Saints and Panthers are incredible to own?? I’m relishing my time at the top of the ranks because I think this team is in my rearview mirror, and it’s closer than it appears.
blurbs.6: Maybe this is a bit harsh to Nick’s team after an okay start, but I’m not sure he’d put his team anywhere else. It’s just tough to like the long-term outlook of this team when the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th-round picks are all injured. The team hasn’t broken 80 points since week 1, the starting RBs are Rhamondre Stevenson and George Holani, and heavy personnel is likely going to need to be deployed for the second week in a row… so naturally he’s gonna beat me this week.
blurbs.7: Yet another week on top. The wax wings are starting to melt as the bye weeks and injuries pile up but, as precarious as my perch is, I still sit atop it. No weeks below 115 yet, and I’m undefeated despite facing a median winner every week so far. So, look only at my standings and my total points and my playoff percentage. Just don’t look at my RB room next week with Walker on bye. I’m serious, don’t look at it.
blurbs.8: What even is there to say at this point? The worst start in league history in terms of points scored, and not even a lame win in a shit week to show for it. You’d think this would prompt some kind of trade or big move from Cam but he’s mostly just sitting here, wallowing in this bath full of poop he’s created for himself. At least he’s progressively scoring more each week; by week 12 he’ll finally break 100 points, at this rate!
blurbs.9: Connor’s team continues its consistent inconsistency. Just when we thought Jeremiyah Love was finally the guy he was picked to be, he goes out and tweaks his ankle and tells his team to not play him. Keep in mind, this 89-point performance is with Bijan scoring almost 30 last night; I shudder to think of the lows this team can reach when the Falcons aren’t incredible.
blurbs.10: A real wonky performance this week, everyone was just kinda there and no one did particularly well. I think you just gotta take this one on the chin and move on to next week, be a goldfish, as it were. I still believe in the core of this team, but past the first 4-5 players things start to look kinda shaky. There are like, two too many Chargers on this team. The double TE strategy is finally catching up to Liam here; who knew a strategy that rarely works and is extremely inconsistent would be a bad thing to rely on?
blurbs.11: The second-straight week where Austin goes 0-2; the world is starting to feel normal again. In weeks where Josh Allen doesn’t score 35+ points, the Machine is completely unremarkable, which is a development by which I am utterly shocked. It’s almost as if this team was doing well, singing its songs and playing its music, when all of a sudden, a dashing man stabbed them in the head with an umbrella and stopped them in their tracks. Better hope you can find that culprit, otherwise it’s curtains for the coming weeks.
blurbs.12: That’s one in the win column, boys! Sure, maybe it’s some type of cosmic prediction that even in his best week, and even as the 2nd scorer, Xander still can’t go 2-0, but Puka’s back, Taylor and Williams keep scoring touchdowns, and $100 Ollie Gordon balled out on the bench just for good measure. It’s a good thing Jalen Hurts has been equally elite, and the Eagles’ offense is a juggernaut once again, because otherwise there’d be cause for some concern! Phew.
